title: Choose the tenant dashboard structure
question: Each option preserves LPE's existing administration system. Choose the layout that should make provisioning, mail flow, and quarantine risk easiest to operate.

options.label: Provisioning ledger
options.thesis: A focused worklist drives domain and account setup, while a compact risk rail keeps delivery and quarantine exceptions impossible to miss.
options.viewport: The header names the tenant; a full-width provisioning list dominates, with a narrow right rail for queue, quarantine, and protocol exceptions.
options.risk: The operational rail must stay selective or it will compete with the primary provisioning task.

options.label: Operations workbench
options.thesis: Domains, accounts, and aliases appear as one actionable tenant inventory, with delivery health compressed into a single decisive status band.
options.viewport: A tenant pulse band stretches across the top; below it, a full-width inventory list is grouped by domain with clear New actions and urgent exceptions inline.
options.risk: The grouped inventory needs disciplined row design to remain scannable with many domains.

options.label: Health-first portfolio
options.thesis: A concise risk overview establishes whether the tenant is safe to operate, then hands off directly into domain and account actions.
options.viewport: A calm top row shows healthy capacity and risky mail-flow signals; two large action panels below lead directly to domain and account provisioning.
options.risk: It may feel more like monitoring than a working dashboard unless the next actions are exceptionally direct.
